name: Latvia
description: Latvia offers expats an appealing blend of historical charm, natural beauty, and a relatively affordable cost of living compared to many Western European nations. Its status as an EU member state provides significant advantages, including freedom of movement within the Schengen Area, making it an attractive destination for those seeking European access without the higher expenses.
longdescription: Expat life in Latvia, particularly in the capital Riga, is characterized by a mix of old-world European charm and modern amenities. The country boasts a rich cultural heritage, evident in its Art Nouveau architecture and vibrant arts scene. The economy is moderately stable, with expected growth, though wages are generally lower than in Western Europe. Society is often described as polite and reserved, with a strong appreciation for nature and tradition. English is commonly spoken in business and tourism sectors, but learning Latvian is highly beneficial for deeper integration into society and public services. Latvia offers a clean environment and low crime rates, contributing to a high quality of life. The cost of living is a significant draw, with housing and daily expenses being considerably lower than in many other EU capitals, attracting remote workers, students, and families.

visas.name: Latvia Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: The Latvia Digital Nomad Visa is a long-stay (Type D) visa designed for non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals who are employed by or self-employed with a company registered in an OECD member country, enabling them to reside and work remotely from Latvia. It allows eligible individuals to legally stay in Latvia for extended periods while performing work for employers or businesses located outside Latvia.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who work remotely for a foreign employer or operate a business registered in an OECD country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The long-stay visa for remote work (Type D visa) does not in itself provide a direct path to permanent residency in Latvia. To apply for permanent residency, individuals would typically need to switch to a different legal basis (e.g., employment with a Latvian company or investment) that explicitly counts towards the required continuous residence period.
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must continue to meet all original eligibility requirements, including maintaining remote work for a foreign employer or foreign-registered business, financial self-sufficiency, and valid health insurance.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Latvia Digital Nomad Visa may be subject to a 15% flat Personal Income Tax (PIT) rate, as suggested by some sources for this visa category, for income earned while residing in Latvia and meeting tax residency criteria.
benefits: Extended stay: Live and work in Latvia for up to one year, with the option to renew for another year.
EU Access: Explore other Schengen countries during your stay for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
Affordable Living: Enjoy a high quality of life at a fraction of the cost compared to Western Europe.
Cultural Immersion: Experience a rich blend of Baltic, Nordic, and European traditions.
Relatively streamlined application process.
required_documents: Valid Passport (valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay, with at least two blank pages)
Completed and Signed Visa Application Form
Recent Passport-Style Photograph (not older than 6 months)
Proof of Health Insurance (valid in Latvia and the Schengen Area with minimum coverage of €42,600)
Documents Certifying Expected Place of Residence in Latvia (e.g., rental agreement, booking confirmation)
Proof of Remote Work Eligibility (employment contract stating remote work, or business registration if self-employed)
Document from tax administration of an OECD member state verifying current employment/self-employment status
Certification by an employer registered in an OECD country regarding prior employment for at least six months (for employees)
Proof of Financial Self-Sufficiency (bank statements, payslips, tax returns demonstrating income)
Clean Criminal Record Certificate (apostilled)
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are complete and translated if necessary.
Complete the online visa application form.
Submit the application and supporting documents at a Latvian embassy, consulate, or a designated visa application center (e.g., VFS Center). An interview may be required.
Pay the state application fee.
Await processing of the application and receive the visa upon approval.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Employment (Work Visa)
visas.description: This permit allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens to reside in Latvia for employment purposes for an extended period. It grants the holder the right to work for a specific employer in a defined position within Latvia, with the possibility of extension.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals from third countries who have secured a job offer from a Latvian employer and meet the specified income and qualification requirements.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A permanent residence permit may be granted after at least five years of legal residence in Latvia with a temporary residence permit, provided the applicant demonstrates sufficient financial means and an A2-level command of the Latvian language. [6, 10, 15]
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit holder must maintain their employment, comply with the required salary thresholds, and fulfill tax payment obligations. [5, 11, 12]
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply. The employer must register the employee in the State Revenue Service and pay all required taxes. [13, 19]
benefits: Legal right to live and work in Latvia.
Access to the Schengen Area for short-term travel (up to 90 days within any 180-day period). [5]
Possibility of family reunification for dependants. [10, 11]
Potential path to permanent residency after five years of legal residence. [6, 10, 15]
Access to eSignature (digital signature included in eID card). [6]
required_documents: Completed and signed residence permit application form. [9, 11, 15, 21]
Valid passport (with at least three months' validity beyond the intended stay and at least two blank pages, copies of identification pages and previously issued visas). [4, 8, 9, 20]
One color passport-sized photograph (3.5 x 4.5 cm). [7, 9, 11, 20]
Invitation from the Latvian employer, approved by the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA/PMLP). [8, 9, 20]
Signed employment contract or binding job offer from a Latvian employer, specifying position, salary, and conditions. [4, 8, 9, 11, 19, 20, 23]
Proof of qualifications (diplomas, professional licenses, certificates, work history), often requiring apostille/legalization and certified Latvian translation. [3, 4, 6, 9, 11]
Proof of accommodation in Latvia. [3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14]
Health insurance policy valid in Latvia and Schengen member states, with a minimum liability limit of €42,600. [3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 18, 21, 22, 23]

Criminal record certificate from the country of origin or residence (for foreigners older than 14 years who have resided there for more than 12 months), if applicable, often requiring apostille/legalization and certified Latvian translation. [4, 6, 9, 11, 13]
Proof of payment of the state fee. [9, 11, 13, 15, 22, 24]
Documents confirming sufficient financial means (e.g., bank statements). [5, 7, 11, 13, 21, 22]
application_process_steps: The Latvian employer registers the job vacancy with the State Employment Agency (NVA) for at least 10 working days to pass a labor market test (unless exempt). [4, 5, 9, 17]
The employer obtains an opinion from the NVA and submits an invitation/sponsorship request for the foreign worker to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA/PMLP). [4, 5, 9, 17]

The foreign national applies for a long-stay (Type D) visa with the right to employment at a Latvian embassy or consulate abroad, submitting required documents and paying the visa fee. [4, 8, 9, 17, 20]

Upon approval of the visa and entry into Latvia (or at the embassy/consulate), the foreigner applies for the temporary residence permit by submitting the full set of documents to the OCMA/PMLP, undergoing an interview, and providing biometric data. [3, 7, 8, 9, 11, 21]
After a positive decision, the temporary residence permit card is issued and collected from the OCMA/PMLP. [8, 9, 11]
The employer registers the employee with the State Revenue Service. [13]

visas.name: EU Blue Card
visas.description: The EU Blue Card in Latvia is a temporary residence and work permit designed for highly qualified non-EU citizens. It allows the holder to live and work in Latvia in a skilled position and simplifies the process for obtaining permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EU citizen with a university degree or at least 5 years of professional experience, who has a valid job offer for highly qualified employment in Latvia with a salary meeting the specified threshold.
visas.path_to_residency_description: EU Blue Card holders can qualify for permanent residency after legally residing in Latvia for at least five years. This period can include residence in other EU Member States as an EU Blue Card holder, provided the last two years were in Latvia. Requirements include sufficient financial means, a place of residence, and sufficient command of Latvian.
visas.renewal_conditions: The same conditions and requirements that led to the initial authorization must continue to be met, including maintaining a valid highly qualified employment contract and meeting salary thresholds. The card can be renewed for two-year periods.
benefits: Fast track to permanent residency and potential EU citizenship.
Family reunification, allowing spouses and children to join immediately with work and study rights.
EU mobility, permitting relocation to other EU countries after 18 months.
Expanded labor rights and freedom to change employers after a certain period.
Access to the same treatment as nationals regarding work, education, social security, and health.
required_documents: Valid work contract or binding job offer for highly qualified employment (at least 1 year duration).
Documents proving higher professional qualifications (university degree of at least 3 years or 5 years of professional experience).
Valid travel document/passport copy.
Application form for a residence permit.
Photograph.
Document confirming sufficient financial means/subsistence (employment contract is typically sufficient).
Proof of health insurance (minimum 42,600 EUR coverage after arrival).
Statement on punishability/clean criminal record from country of citizenship or residence (if resided there over 12 months).
Proof of payment of the state fee.
Proof of residence address (after arrival).
Sponsorship confirmation from the inviting company at the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA).
application_process_steps: Employer obtains approval of an invitation for employment from the local branch of the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA).
Applicant gathers all required documents, including the employment contract, proof of qualifications, health insurance, and criminal record certificate.
Applicant submits the application for a Blue Card to a diplomatic or consular representative office of Latvia abroad, or directly to OCMA if legally residing in Latvia.
Pay the application fee for document examination.
OCMA evaluates the application and issues a decision.
Upon approval, provide biometric data and receive the EU Blue Card; declare place of residence and provide radiologist's report in Latvia.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Studies (Student Visa)
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Studies (Student Visa) in Latvia allows non-EU citizens to reside in Latvia for the purpose of full-time academic studies at an accredited higher education institution or participation in study programs. It grants the holder the right to live in Latvia for the duration of their studies.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who have been accepted into a full-time study program at an accredited higher education institution in Latvia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After completing studies, students can apply for a temporary residence permit for up to 9 months to seek employment or start a business. Upon securing employment, they can apply for a temporary residence permit for employment. After 5 years of legal residence in Latvia with a temporary residence permit, they may be eligible to apply for permanent residency, provided they meet continuity, income, and A2-level Latvian language proficiency criteria.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the original basis of residence (study status), submit documents not later than 40 days before current permit expires, and present a valid health insurance policy and fluorography/x-ray results issued in Latvia.
benefits: Opportunity to obtain a globally recognized degree within the EU.
Access to the Schengen Area, allowing travel to 25+ countries.
Permission to work part-time during studies to support living expenses.
Pathway to long-term residency and potential permanent residency after studies.
Relatively affordable tuition fees and living costs compared to other EU countries.
required_documents: Valid passport (original and copy, valid for at least 3 months longer than the planned residence permit term)
Definite sample form for a residence permit request
One recent passport-size photograph (3x4 cm)
Official invitation from the university (filed by the university representative at OCMA)
Study agreement with the Latvian educational institution
Document confirming the necessary subsistence: official bank statement (issued within the last 3 months) showing at least €780 per month for the first year (€9360 total)
Document confirming the envisaged place of residence in Latvia and the rights to stay there (e.g., rental agreement or university dormitory confirmation)
Health insurance policy (valid in Latvia, minimum coverage €42,600)
Criminal report / statement on punishability issued by a competent institution of the citizenship or host country, if resided there longer than 12 months (valid for 6 months from issue date)
Documents confirming previous education (legalized and translated if issued abroad)
Academic Information Center (AIC) decision/certificate (if issued)
Proof of state duty payment
application_process_steps: Receive an official invitation from a recognized Latvian university (the university files this at the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs - OCMA).
Gather all required documents, ensuring translations are notarized where necessary.
Book an in-person appointment at the nearest Latvian embassy or consulate (or OCMA if eligible to apply in Latvia).
Submit the complete application package and attend an interview with a Consular Officer.
Pay the application fees for the residence permit.
If the residence permit is approved, apply for a D-type (long-stay) visa (if required by nationality) to enter Latvia, then register the residence permit at OCMA within 30 days of arrival.

visas.name: Latvia Investor Visa (Golden Visa) - Investment in Equity Capital of a Latvian Company
visas.description: The Latvia Investor Visa, also known as the Golden Visa, is a program for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who invest in the equity capital of a Latvian company. It grants a temporary residence permit for up to five years, allowing the investor and their family to reside in Latvia and travel freely within the Schengen Area.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign investor seeking European residency through a capital contribution to a Latvian company, desiring Schengen mobility and a pathway to permanent residency and citizenship.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of legal temporary residence, investors may apply for permanent residency. After 10 years of legal residence (5 years temporary + 5 years permanent), it is possible to apply for Latvian citizenship through naturalization, subject to fulfilling language skills and other integration requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: The investment must be maintained, and the company must continue to meet the qualifying criteria (e.g., tax payments if applicable). An additional payment of EUR 5,000 to the state budget is required upon renewal of the temporary residence permit. Annual re-registration of the ID card in Latvia is required.
visas.tax_implications: Standard Latvian resident tax rules apply. No specific special tax treatment is noted for this visa category.
benefits: Visa-free access to the Schengen Area.
No minimum stay required to maintain the residence permit.
Path to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years of legal residence.
Dependents (spouse, minor children, persons under trusteeship) can be included in the application.
Permitted to live and work in Latvia.
required_documents: Full copy of passport (foreigner certifies validity).
Definite sample form for a residence permit request.
Photography.
Document certifying necessary subsistence (e.g., bank statements).
Document confirming state duty payment (for investment-related fees and application fees).
Company documentation and proof of share capital investment.
Legal source of funds documentation.
Health insurance policy meeting minimum coverage requirements.
Criminal record documentation (where required by route or personal history).
Marriage and birth certificates if family members are included (and other relationship-confirming documents, e.g., permission of other parent for minors).
application_process_steps: Choose a qualifying investment option in a Latvian company's equity capital.
Your inviter (the company) must approve an invitation letter at the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA).
Prepare all required documents, including proof of investment, subsistence, and clean criminal record.
Submit the application and documents to a Latvian embassy/consulate or directly to the OCMA in Latvia.
Undergo a due diligence process by the OCMA.
Upon approval, visit Latvia in person within three months to collect your temporary residence permit ID card and make the required state budget payment.

visas.name: Latvia Investor Visa (Golden Visa) - Real Estate Purchase
visas.description: The Latvia Investor Visa, commonly known as the Golden Visa, is officially a temporary residence permit program offering non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens the opportunity to gain residency in Latvia through a qualifying investment in real estate. It provides a pathway to living in the EU and visa-free travel within the Schengen Area.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU, non-EEA, and non-Swiss citizens interested in obtaining a temporary residence permit in Latvia by investing in real estate.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of temporary residency, investors may apply for permanent residency, which requires residing in Latvia for at least 4 out of the 5 years (with absences not exceeding 6 months per year) and passing a basic Latvian language exam (A2 level). Citizenship may be applied for after 10 years of legal residence (5 years on TRP + 5 years on PR), requiring further language, culture, and history exams, and proof of stable income.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintain the qualifying investment, pay an additional state fee of EUR 5,000 to the state budget, and meet general residence permit requirements.
visas.tax_implications: Residents are subject to tax on their worldwide income. Real property tax is levied at 1.5% of the cadastral value of land and buildings, with residential properties taxed between 0.2% and 0.6%. No special tax exemptions are explicitly mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Visa-free travel across the Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
No mandatory minimum stay requirement to maintain temporary residency status.
Ability to include spouse and minor children in the same application.
Potential path to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years of legal residence.
Opportunity for passive income through property rentals.
required_documents: Valid passport/travel document
Proof of investment (property purchase documents, proof of bank transfer)
Certificate verifying property market value meets requirements
Proof of sufficient financial means to subsist (bank statements showing at least €26,640 for main applicant, additional funds for family members)
Health insurance policy
Proof of legal place of residence in Latvia (Land Register entry or lease agreement)
One passport-size photo
Receipt of payment of state fees
Documents confirming kinship for family members (marriage/birth certificates)
Consent from the non-accompanying parent for minor children (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Choose and make a qualifying real estate investment.
Gather and prepare all required documents.
Submit the application and documents to a Latvian embassy/consulate or directly to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA) in Latvia.
Undergo a due diligence process.
Receive approval for the temporary residence permit.
Visit Latvia within 3 months of approval to collect the residence permit ID card.

visas.name: Latvia Investor Visa (Golden Visa) - Bank Deposit
visas.description: The Latvia Investor Visa (Golden Visa) - Bank Deposit program offers non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and their families a temporary residence permit in Latvia in exchange for a qualifying investment. It provides a pathway to EU residency, allowing visa-free travel within the Schengen Area and eventually leading to permanent residency and citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens seeking a secure and structured investment route to gain temporary residency in a stable EU country with potential for long-term residency and citizenship.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of continuous temporary residency, investors can apply for a permanent residence permit. After 10 years of legal residence (5 years temporary + 5 years permanent), they may apply for Latvian citizenship, subject to language proficiency and integration requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintain the investment for at least five years, pay an additional state fee of €5,000 upon renewal (after the initial 5-year period), visit Latvia at least once per year for ID card renewal, maintain valid health insurance, and have no criminal convictions.
visas.tax_implications: Latvia does not charge corporate income tax on profits that are reinvested into the business; a standard 20% tax rate applies when profits are distributed as dividends. Standard resident tax rules apply if residing in Latvia for more than 180 days. Capital gains tax may apply to any returns from the bank deposit.
benefits: Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area.
No minimum stay requirements to maintain the visa, only an annual visit for renewal.
Inclusion of spouse and dependent children under 18 in the same application.
Potential for permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years.
Access to Latvian education and healthcare systems.
required_documents: Valid passport (minimum 3-6 months validity beyond intended residence commencement)
Application form for a residence permit (from PMLP)
Passport-size photos (biometric format, taken no later than 3 months ago)
Certificate of absence of criminal record from all countries of residence for the last 5 years (apostilled/legalized, translated to Latvian, not older than 6 months)

Proof of sufficient financial means/solvency to support applicant and dependents (e.g., bank statements, minimum income declaration: at least €960 per month for main applicant, €500 for each adult dependent, €150 for each child)
Proof of planned accommodation in Latvia (e.g., rental contract, property deed)
Health insurance policy valid in Latvia and the Schengen Area, covering the entire duration of stay with minimum coverage of €43,000-€45,000
Document confirming state duty payment
Bank confirmation letter regarding the €280,000 subordinated deposit, fixed for at least 5 years
Source of funds documentation for the invested amount
Marriage certificate (if applicable, for spouse)
Birth certificates (if applicable, for dependent children)
application_process_steps: Engage legal support and undergo initial due diligence checks.
Open a bank account in Latvia and deposit a minimum of €280,000 as a subordinated deposit for a fixed term of 5 years.
Gather and legalize all required documents, including translations into Latvian where necessary.
Submit the application to a Latvian diplomatic mission (embassy/consulate) or directly to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP) in Latvia.
Provide biometric data (fingerprints) in Latvia or at certain embassies.
Upon approval, pay the €25,000 government fee and travel to Latvia to collect the temporary residence permit ID cards for all included family members.

visas.name: Latvia Investor Visa (Golden Visa) - Purchase of Government Bonds
visas.description: The Latvia Investor Visa (also known as Golden Visa) via government bonds allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens to obtain a temporary residence permit in Latvia by investing in special purpose, interest-free government bonds. This program grants the holder and their family the right to live, work, and study in Latvia, providing visa-free travel within the Schengen Area and a pathway to permanent residency and eventual citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EU, non-EEA, or non-Swiss citizen with a clean criminal record seeking an EU residence permit through a secure investment, with the aim of gaining Schengen access and a potential long-term path to permanent residency and citizenship.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding a temporary residence permit for five years, applicants may apply for a permanent residence permit. Eligibility for permanent residency may require fulfilling conditions such as maintaining the investment, language skills, and significant physical residency (e.g., 183 days per year) in Latvia. After five years of holding a permanent residence permit (total of 10 years of legal residency), individuals may apply for Latvian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew the temporary residence permit, the investor must maintain the €250,000 investment in government bonds, pay taxes, and visit Latvia at least once a year to renew the resident permit ID card, continuing to fulfill all established requirements.
visas.tax_implications: Individuals become tax residents if they have a permanent place of residence in Latvia or are present in Latvia for 183 days or more in any 12-month period. Residents are subject to tax on their worldwide income, while non-residents pay taxes on income derived from Latvia. Standard tax rates apply to employment income, business income, capital gains, and investment income. [cite: 4 (from previous search)]
benefits: Visa-free travel within the Schengen Area.
Right to live, work, and study in Latvia and the EU.
Pathway to permanent residency after 5 years and citizenship after 10 years.
Investment is risk-free and refunded after 5 years by the Latvian government.
Family reunification, allowing spouse and minor children to be included.
required_documents: A full copy of a passport (foreigner certifies the validity of the document).
An application on a specific form for the request of a residence permit.
Photo (passport-size 35x45 mm).
A document certifying the necessary subsistence (500 EUR per month for an adult, 150 EUR per month for a minor).

A statement issued by the competent institution of the state of citizenship or residence regarding the criminal record (for a foreigner older than 14 years of age), if a foreigner has resided therein for more than 12 months.
A payment document attesting to the payment of the State fee.
Documents attesting kinship (if applying with family members).

Notarially certified permission or a permission signed in the presence of an official of the Office or Mission regarding consent to the travel of the child to the Republic of Latvia of the parent who does not enter together with the child (if applicable).
Proof of health insurance covering Latvia and the Schengen area.
Undertaking to purchase Government Financial Instruments.
Evidence of Residential Address (through ownership or rental in Latvia).
application_process_steps: Consultation and selection of the government bonds investment route.
Undergo a due diligence check and prepare all required documents, including a valid passport, application form, photos, proof of subsistence, and criminal record statement.
Submit the application with supporting documents to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA) or a Latvian consulate abroad.
OCMA reviews the application (typically 1-3 months), and upon a positive decision, further information on bond acquisition is provided.
Acquire the €250,000 interest-free government bonds from a current account in a Latvian credit institution and make the €38,000 state budget payment.
Visit Latvia for biometric data collection and to receive the 5-year temporary residence permit ID card.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification in Latvia allows close family members of Latvian citizens, non-citizens, or permanent residents to reside together in Latvia. It also applies to family members of individuals granted refugee or subsidiary protection status in Latvia, enabling them to live, work, and access social benefits in the country.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are spouses, unmarried minor children (under 18), and in some cases, retired parents, of individuals who hold Latvian citizenship, non-citizen status, or a permanent or specific temporary residence permit in Latvia, seeking to live together.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 5 years of continuous residence in Latvia with a temporary residence permit (with at least 183 days per year spent in the country), applicants may apply for permanent residency. This requires demonstrating Latvian language proficiency at A2 level and passing a Constitution and history test. After 5 years of permanent residence, eligibility for Latvian citizenship becomes accessible.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintaining the conditions under which the permit was granted, including sufficient income and valid health insurance. For children, if still under 18, the permit is extended for 5 years. After turning 18, they retain the permit if living with parents, unmarried, and residing in Latvia.
benefits: Right to live together in Latvia with family members.
Potential for faster processing compared to some other immigration programs.
Access to certain social benefits and rights.
Provides a clear path towards obtaining permanent residency and eventually Latvian citizenship.
Allows spouses and minor children to obtain a residence permit without direct involvement in specific investment programs if the main applicant has one.
required_documents: Completed application form for temporary residence permit
Valid travel document (passport) with copies of all pages
Color photograph (3.5 by 4.5 centimeters)
Criminal record clearance certificate from the country of residence for the past year (for third-country nationals over 14 who resided there for more than 12 months)
Documentary proof of sufficient means of subsistence (e.g., income proof)
Health insurance policy valid in Latvia
Proof of housing in Latvia (e.g., rental agreement or property ownership certificate)
Official invitation approved by the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP)
Documents proving family relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate), legalized and translated into Latvian
Notarized consent from the other parent for minors if moving with only one parent (or signed in presence of an officer)
Copy of domestic (internal) passport (if applicable)
application_process_steps: The inviter obtains an official invitation for the family member from the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA/PMLP) in Latvia.
The inviter provides personal information about the family member, identification, contact details, and pays a state fee.

The family member abroad applies to the Latvian embassy or consular office, submitting the completed temporary residence permit application and required documents, including a valid passport and obtaining a Type D visa if necessary.
After receiving the visa (if applicable), the family member travels to Latvia.
Upon arrival in Latvia, the family member must visit the OCMA to receive their temporary residence permit and pay the associated state fee.
Submit health certificate and valid health insurance policy upon receiving the temporary residence permit.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Self-Employed Persons/Individual Merchants
visas.description: This Temporary Residence Permit is for non-EU nationals who intend to conduct economic activities as self-employed persons or individual merchants in Latvia. It allows the holder to reside in Latvia and operate their own business, with different validity periods and financial thresholds depending on whether they are registered as a self-employed person (up to 1 year) or an individual merchant in the Commercial Register (up to 5 years).
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU nationals looking to establish and operate their own business or act as a sole trader in Latvia, requiring a verified business plan.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A long-term resident status (permanent residency) may be granted after at least five years of legal residence in Latvia, provided the applicant has sufficient financial means to support themselves and dependants, a sufficient command of Latvian, and a registered place of residence in Latvia. [cite: 5 in prev, 7 in prev]
visas.renewal_conditions: For a self-employed person, the permit can be renewed if self-employed activities are maintained, and tax payments to the state and local government budget are at least €9,960 per year (or €800 per month for an incomplete fiscal year). For an individual merchant, renewal requires annual tax payments of not less than €14,230 per year (or €1,150 per month for an incomplete fiscal year). An updated business plan checked by a sworn auditor is required from the second year of operation. Annual registration is required for permits valid for more than one year, 30-90 days before the end of each annual period. [cite: 2, 4, 5 in prev, 7 in prev]
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this permit are subject to Latvia's standard tax regulations for resident individuals and businesses, with renewal contingent on meeting specific annual tax payment thresholds to the state and local government budgets. These are distinct from the special tax regime for digital nomads. [cite: 2 in prev, 4 in prev, 5 in prev, 7 in prev]
benefits: Right to legally reside in Latvia.
Visa-free travel and stay within the Schengen Area.
Ability to engage in any additional self-employed activity.
Option for family reunification with dependants.
Potential path to permanent residency after five years of legal residence.
required_documents: Valid travel document (passport copy).
Completed application form for a residence permit request.
Passport-sized photograph.
Document certifying the necessary subsistence (minimum €2554 per month for the applicant; €500 per month for an adult dependant; €150 per month for a minor dependant).
Document confirming the prospective place of residence in Latvia. [cite: 4 in prev]
Document certifying the payment of the State fee.
Business plan for the expected period of activity, approved by a sworn auditor. [cite: 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 in prev, 2]

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Retirees
visas.description: This Temporary Residence Permit allows financially self-sufficient foreign nationals, specifically pensioners from visa-free countries, to reside in Latvia for an extended period. It is designed for individuals who can demonstrate a stable monthly pension income and do not require employment in Latvia. The permit offers a pathway to long-term residency within the European Union's Schengen Area.
visas.target_applicant: Retirees aged 65 or above, or who have reached the statutory retirement age in Latvia, holding a passport from a country with visa-free access to Latvia, and possessing a stable, regular pension income.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of holding a temporary residence permit, individuals may apply for permanent residency. To qualify for permanent residency, applicants typically need to have resided legally in Latvia for at least four out of the five years, demonstrate sufficient financial means, and prove Latvian language proficiency (minimum A2 level) and knowledge of the country's history and national anthem. [cite: 11 (from previous search results), 13 (from previous search results)] After a total of ten years of legal residency (five temporary, five permanent), eligibility for Latvian citizenship may arise, requiring advanced language proficiency (B1) and generally renouncing previous citizenship (with exceptions). [cite: 6 (from previous search results), 11 (from previous search results)]
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain the required pension income and meet the conditions under which the permit was granted. An annual visit to Latvia is required to renew the residence card. [cite: 5 (from previous search results), 7 (from previous search results)]
visas.tax_implications: Latvia has a flat personal income tax rate of 20%. Residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed only on income derived from Latvia. Double tax treaties may apply, allowing taxes to be paid in another country if such a treaty exists, avoiding double taxation through credit or exemption. [cite: 5 (from previous search results)]
benefits: Freedom of movement within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Potential path to permanent residency and eventually Latvian citizenship.
Ability to include spouse and dependent children in the application.
Access to Latvia's public healthcare system for residents.
No minimum stay requirement for renewal, only an annual visit to renew the residence card.
required_documents: Full copy of a valid passport (foreigner certifies validity)
Definite sample form for a residence permit request
Passport-size photograph
Document certifying necessary subsistence (proof of pension income, e.g., pension statements)
Document confirming state duty payment
Proof of accommodation/place of residence in Latvia (e.g., lease agreement or land register entry)
Health insurance policy valid in Latvia and the Schengen Area (minimum coverage of €42,600 is generally required for TRP) [cite: 8, 12 (from previous search results)]

Certificate of no criminal record from the country of citizenship or long-term residence (for individuals aged 14 and older, though some sources indicate it might not be strictly required for this category) [cite: 5 (from previous search results), 6 (from previous search results)]
Marriage certificate (if applying with spouse) [cite: 5 (from previous search results)]
Birth certificates/relationship confirming documents (if applying with minor children/dependants)

application_process_steps: Gather all required documentation, including passport, photos, proof of pension, health insurance, and accommodation.
Complete and sign the official residence permit application form.
Legalize foreign official documents with an apostille or legalization, and translate into English, Russian, or Latvian if not already in these languages.

Submit the complete application pack and pay the state duty at a Latvian diplomatic mission abroad (embassy/consulate) or directly to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (PMLP) in Latvia. [cite: 4, 9, 12 (from previous search results)]

Upon approval, travel to Latvia (if applied from abroad), provide biometric data, and collect the temporary residence card (eID card). [cite: 4, 10 (from previous search results)]

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Latvian citizenship by descent operates on the *jus sanguinis* (right of blood) principle. It is primarily available to individuals who can prove that one of their ancestors held Latvian citizenship on or before June 17, 1940 (the date of Soviet occupation), or who left Latvia between 1940-1990 to escape occupation. Descendants of such persons may also apply. Dual citizenship is permitted in specific circumstances, particularly for citizens of EU, EEA, NATO member states, Australia, Brazil, New Zealand, or with special permission from the Cabinet of Ministers. Required documents typically include birth and marriage certificates to establish lineage.

Naturalization.desc: Naturalization is generally possible after a cumulative period of 10 years of permanent legal residency in Latvia, which includes 5 years with a temporary residence permit followed by 5 years with a permanent residence permit. Applicants must be at least 15 years old. Key requirements include demonstrating a good command of the Latvian language (A2 or B1 level, through testing), knowing the text of the National Anthem, the basics of Latvian history and culture, and the fundamental principles of the Constitution. Applicants must also prove a legal source of income and typically undergo a criminal record check.

Birthright.desc: Since January 1, 2020, Latvian citizenship is granted to all children born in Latvia, regardless of their parents' 'non-citizen' status, unless both parents explicitly agree for the child to acquire another citizenship. If a child is born to at least one Latvian citizen parent, they are automatically granted Latvian citizenship, irrespective of their birthplace, provided the birth is registered with the Latvian government.

Spouse and Family.desc: Marriage to a Latvian citizen does not automatically grant citizenship. However, the spouse of a Latvian citizen can apply for a temporary residence permit. This permit is initially issued for one year and can be renewed for subsequent periods. After at least five years of continuous legal residence in Latvia, demonstrating a genuine marital relationship, the spouse may apply for permanent residency. Citizenship by naturalization can then be pursued after fulfilling the total 10-year residency requirement and meeting all other naturalization criteria, including language and civics tests. Children born to Latvian citizens acquire citizenship automatically.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Latvia employs a progressive PIT system. As of January 1, 2025, a rate of 25.5% applies to annual income up to EUR 105,300, and a rate of 33% applies to income exceeding this threshold. An additional 3% PIT rate applies to the portion of an individual's total annual income that exceeds EUR 200,000. Income from capital, including capital gains, is generally taxed at 25.5%.
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** Latvia has a unique corporate tax system where profits are not taxed when earned but only when distributed (e.g., as dividends). The standard CIT rate on distributed profits is 20%, which translates to an effective rate of 25% (20/80 on the net distribution). Reinvested profits are exempt from CIT. Micro-enterprise tax (MBT) is an alternative regime for qualifying entities, taxed at 25% on turnover.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate in Latvia is 21%. Reduced rates include 12% for items such as medicines, medical products, baby food, hotel services, district heating, and fresh fruits, berries, and vegetables. A 5% rate applies to printed and online books, educational materials, and certain press publications. A 0% rate is applied to exports and intra-EU supplies of goods to VAT-registered customers.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Riga is considered affordable compared to Western European capitals. A single person's estimated monthly expenses (excluding rent) range from €1,026 to €1,290. Rent for a one-bedroom apartment in the city center is approximately €500-€700 per month, and €300-€500 outside the center. Utilities can range from €160-€280 monthly, and groceries for a single person average €50-€70 per week.
*   **Language:** While Latvian is the official language, English is widely spoken in the capital's commercial and tourist areas. Russian is also prevalent due to historical ties. However, learning Latvian is crucial for full integration and interacting with public services.
*   **Safety:** Latvia generally has low crime rates, contributing to a sense of security for residents.
*   **Residency and Registration:** Non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals can obtain temporary residence permits through investment programs (e.g., Golden Visa) with investments starting from €50,000 in company equity or €250,000 in real estate. While initial permits may have no minimum stay, qualifying for permanent residency requires living in Latvia for at least 183 days per year for four out of five years, paying taxes, and passing a basic Latvian language test (A2 level). Stricter rules for permanent residency were introduced in 2024-2025, emphasizing continuous residence, language proficiency, financial stability, tax compliance, and registered accommodation.
